significance: A Shvetambara complex of four shrines at Badridas Temple Street, built in 1867 by the philanthropist Rai Badridas Bahadoor Mookim and consecrated by Acharya Kalyansuri. The main shrine to Shitalanatha is famous for mirror-inlaid pillars, stained glass, mosaic and glass chandeliers, and a ghee lamp said to have burned since 1867; the complex also holds the footprints of the monks Jinadattasuri and Jinkushalsuri.
